MICHEL ZOOBRIDSKY, aged 22 years, born in 
Jelantoon, Manchuria, of Polish parents. 

From the age of 9 until 1931, lived in Harbin 
where he was educated and on leaving school was employed 
as a musician in various cabarets and cinema theatres. 

Went to Shanghai in October,1931; after ten days 
went to Harbin where he spent two weeks and then returned 
to Shanghai. . 

After a few days went to Canton via Swatow where 
he was unable to fir ' work and later stowed away on a ship 
to Manila where he landed without being detected. 

Remained in Manila playing itn the orchestra of the Russian 
Dancing School, was given permission by the Manila Police to 
remain there provided he was employed. After the closing 
of the Dancing School, he was sent back to Shanghai by 
Police. Arrived in Shanghai by s.s."?resident Taft" on 
31.10.32. Stayed in Shanghai for about a month, but was 
unable to find work and set out for Canton with a friend 
named Nelubin. Was unable to find work in Canton and came 
to Hong Kong on 10.1.33. He reported to Police Headquarters, 
Hong Kong and was later sent away to Canton. On 16.1.33 he 
again arrived in the Colony and was charged under the 
Passport Ordinance and sentenced to 14 days Hard Labour and 
ordered to be expelled from the Colony. He returned to the 
Colony again on 29.3.33, was charged and sentenced to two 


months Hard Labour for a breach of the Passport Regulations, 


and for disobeying his expulsion order. 
The Governor in Council approved his banishment for 
ten years on 17.4.33- 
He states that when he was returned to Shanghai by 
the Manila Police, the papers he had in his possession were 


vise by the Chinese Consul at Manila and are now in the 


possession of the Chinese Passport Authorities in Shanghai. 


He states that he has many friends in Shanghai | 


re 


was BS ca 


and that the following will take care of him if he returns 
to that port:- 
i. VICTOR VOLMENSKY, musician, 42 Route Vallon. 
2. INOKENTI ZAVISCHA-CHARNEY, musician, living at 
either Happy Terrace or Tracy Terrace, Avenue Joffre. 
He states that as he is a Pole, he has never been registered 


by the Russian Emmigration Committee, Shanghai.

1933年5月15日。

先生：

谨此确认收到阁下5月4日的 C.I.D.792/33 号信函及附件，以及5月11日的电报，电文如下：

“参照我5月4日关于 Michel Zoobridsky 的信件，请紧急复电。”

以下回复已于5月13日发出：

“参照阁下来电，护照当局拒绝 Zoobridsky 进入上海。”

经与中国护照当局接洽，他们在考虑此事后表示，拒绝允许 Zoobridsky 进入上海，因为他被视为不受欢迎分子，且在上海无生计来源。

据 Zoobridsky 称，若他返回上海，V. Volmensky 先生和 L. Zavischa-Charney 先生两人将照顾他。其中前者目前不在本市。后者及 V. Volmensky 的母亲已受到询问，看他们是否愿意向中国当局提供书面担保，但两人均未如承诺般向本部门传达其决定。

Subject (in full) Letter from the Inspector General of Police, Hongkong, re:
Michel Zoobridsky.
Made by D.S.Prokofiev Forwarded by Q Bkm S.I.
With reference to the letter dated May 4, 1933 from the
Inspector General of Police, Hongkong, on the subject of Michel
Zoobridsky who is now in the House of Detention in that city
pending deportation, Mr.H.Y.Yuin, Officer i/c of the Shanghai Pub-
lic Safety Bureau Passport Examination Office, was interviewed by
the undersigned on May 12 with a view to ascertaining whether
the above named individual will be re-admitted to Shanghai in
the case of his deportation to this port.
Mr.Yuin replied in the negative and gave the following
reasons:-
1. On the strength of the information contained in
Zoobridsky's own statement he is to be considered
as an undesirable;
2. There is no proof that he formerly resided in
Shanghai, as he is not registered with the Pub-
lic Safety Bureau, or the Polish Legation or with
local Russian Emigrants Organizations;
3. There is no proof that he has any means of sup-
port in Shanghai.
The two persons - Mr. V. Volmensky and Mr.I. Zavissha-

由 D.S. Prokofiev 撰写 由 Q Bkm S.I. 转呈

参照香港警务处处长1933年5月4日关于 Michel Zoobridsky 的来信，此人目前在该市的拘留所等待递解出境。为此，具名者于5月12日会见了上海市公安局护照查验处负责人 H.Y. Yuin 先生，以查明在上述人员被递解至本口岸的情况下，是否会被重新允许进入上海。
Yuin 先生予以否定回答，并给出以下理由：
1. 根据 Zoobridsky 本人陈述中所载信息，他被视为不受欢迎分子；
2. 没有证据证明他以前居住在上海，因为他未在公安局、波兰公使馆或当地俄罗斯侨民组织注册；
3. 没有证据证明他在上海有任何生计来源。
据 Zoobridsky 称，若他返回上海，V. Volmensky 先生和 I. Zavissha-Charney 先生两人将照顾他。其中前者目前不在本市。Zavischa-Charney 先生（音乐家，居住在瓦伦路79号10室）和 V. Volmensky 的母亲（居住在瓦伦路42号1室）已于5月11日接受问询，并承诺于次日告知具名者，他们是否愿意向中国护照当局提供针对 Zoobridsky 的书面担保，但截至目前，他们尚未这样做。

pages.en:
MICHEL ZOOBRIDSKY, aged 22 years, born in
Jelantoon, Manchuria, of Polish parents.
From the age of 9 until 1931, lived in Harbin
where he was educated and on leaving school was employed
as a musician in various cabarets and cinema theatres.
Went to Shanghai in October,1931; after ten days
went to Harbin where he spent two weeks and then returned
to Shanghai.
After a few days went to Canton via Swatow where
he was unable to fir ' work and later stowed away on a ship
to Manila where he landed without being detected.
Remained in Manila playing in the orchestra of the Russian
Dancing School, was given permission by the Manila Police to
remain there provided he was employed. After the closing
of the Dancing School, he was sent back to Shanghai by
Police. Arrived in Shanghai by s.s."President Taft" on
31.10.32. Stayed in Shanghai for about a month, but was
unable to find work and set out for Canton with a friend
named Nelubin. Was unable to find work in Canton and came
to Hong Kong on 10.1.33. He reported to Police Headquarters,
Hong Kong and was later sent away to Canton. On 16.1.33 he
again arrived in the Colony and was charged under the
Passport Ordinance and sentenced to 14 days Hard Labour and
ordered to be expelled from the Colony. He returned to the
Colony again on 29.3.33, was charged and sentenced to two
months Hard Labour for a breach of the Passport Regulations,
and for disobeying his expulsion order.
The Governor in Council approved his banishment for
ten years on 17.4.33.
He states that when he was returned to Shanghai by
the Manila Police, the papers he had in his possession were
visé by the Chinese Consul at Manila and are now in the
possession of the Chinese Passport Authorities in Shanghai.
He states that he has many friends in Shanghai
and
pages.zh:
MICHEL ZOOBRIDSKY，22岁，出生于满洲里 Jelantoon（音译），父母为波兰人。
从9岁到1931年，居住在哈尔滨，在那里接受教育，离校后曾在各种歌舞厅和电影院担任乐师。
1931年10月前往上海；十天后前往哈尔滨，在那里逗留了两周，然后返回上海。
几天后，经汕头前往广州，在那里找不到工作，后来偷渡上一艘前往马尼拉的船只，并在未被发现的情况下登陆。
留在马尼拉，在俄罗斯舞蹈学校的乐队中演奏，获马尼拉警方许可，只要受雇即可留居。舞蹈学校关闭后，他被警方遣送回上海。于1932年10月31日乘“塔夫脱总统号”轮船抵达上海。在上海停留约一个月，但找不到工作，便与一位名叫 Nelubin 的朋友动身前往广州。在广州找不到工作，于1933年1月10日来到香港。他向香港警察总部报到，随后被送往广州。1933年1月16日他再次抵达该殖民地，因违反《护照条例》被起诉，判处14天苦役，并被命令驱逐出该殖民地。他于1933年3月29日再次返回该殖民地，因违反护照规定及不服从驱逐令被起诉，判处两个月苦役。
总督会同行政局于1933年4月17日批准将他放逐十年。
他称，当马尼拉警方将他遣返回上海时，他所持有的文件已由马尼拉的中国领事签证，目前这些文件在上海的中国护照当局手中。
他称，他在上海有许多朋友，并且
